independent.summary: The run-join gate only requires ONE line in a short-line run to carry a schedule signal, and WEEKDAY_RE/MONTH_RE match ordinary nav wording ('Sunday Services', 'May'). In the Puppeteer path nav/header/footer are deliberately NOT removed (scraper.js:283-287) and innerText separates sibling blocks with a single '\n' (scraper.js:310-314), so a menu run such as Home/About/Sunday Services/Give/Events/Contact becomes one ~46-char paragraph that clears keepPara's 20-char floor and enters chunks — chrome that was dropped before. This is exactly the failure the module header claims the gate prevents ('Nav menus are runs of short lines too; none of them says 7:00 pm') and it breaks the item's 'nav and footer chrome stays excluded as it is today' requirement for JS-rendered sites; no fixture exercises the single-newline innerText shape, only the cheerio path where nav/footer are stripped.

The test named "the page's own chrome is still excluded" asserts only 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'Share' and 'Top', all of which sit inside the fixture's <footer>, which textFromFixture removes before extraction — so it passes regardless of this change, and the mobile-menu claim in its own comment (short header <div> lines still falling to the 20-char floor, i.e. 'About'/'Contact') is never asserted.
